title: Say No
coreMove: Protective refusal is not contempt; it keeps time, attention, and care available for the work and people you already chose, with a whole mind.

exampleSpecs.audience: director protecting one chosen project from attractive side grants
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small blank card makes the cost of another yes visible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A close desk moment shows Jordan using Buffett-like selectivity without a live decision.

exampleSpecs.audience: event lead locating the first overcommitment
exampleSpecs.stakes: focus was spent by one attractive addition after the program was full
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Open after the event and locate the first extra yes that spent focus.

exampleSpecs.domain: consulting email written during a crowded client week
exampleSpecs.audience: consultant catching her own people-pleasing mid-message
exampleSpecs.stakes: the early catch matters more than the polished refusal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The protagonist catches a false yes in the draft before it becomes debt.

exampleSpecs.domain: clinic budget memo refusing an added program
exampleSpecs.audience: director using a written artifact to carry the no
exampleSpecs.stakes: the memo refuses a good-looking program to protect current care
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A written refusal names the good request and the better yes it protects.

exampleSpecs.domain: two product leads responding to the same investor feature request
exampleSpecs.audience: leaders comparing focus and appeasement under investor pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: one refusal protects focus while one agreeable yes fractures the product
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A product lead turns an attractive request into a focus test.

exampleSpecs.domain: mentor conversation before a donor call
exampleSpecs.audience: director who confuses refusal with selfishness
exampleSpecs.stakes: a peer reframes no as protection for service
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Gerard gives Jordan a quotable reframe in one conversation.
